correctness.rationale: Reconstructed complete prime-factor proof, including parity and t^2 reduction for odd m, sharp Euler-product exclusions of supports at most three, forcing primes 2,3,5 and r=7,11,13 for four-support m, strict r(16-r)/24>1 exclusion for exponent d>=2, and monotone-ratio bounds a<=4,b<=3,c<=2. Exact integer verifier replayed all 72 bounded cases and independent totient/tau values; optional direct regression through m=50000 is explicitly not an infinite proof. Boundary m=1 is excluded by the odd argument.

originality.rationale: The new implication is unconditional completeness at omega(m)=4. In the focal source, Theorem 6 proves only omega(m)>=4 and Theorem 7 classifies solutions under the extra assumptions that the prime divisors are 2,3,5,p and that p has exponent one. The present prime-product and exponent-ratio argument proves those assumptions for every four-support solution; a 72-case exact check then finishes. Searches and prior records yielded no wider theorem. Residual possibility of unindexed prior equivalent work remains.
residual_risks: An unindexed publication or equivalently formulated result might prove the unconditional first-support classification.
The same three individual numerical examples are already in the focal paper; the new content is solely their unconditional completeness across the minimal-support layer.

value.rationale: The minimum number of distinct primes is the first structural layer in the source equation, and prior Theorems 6 and 7 leave open whether their prescribed prime family exhausts it. Removing the support/exponent hypotheses resolves that natural exact census, proves the last prime is squarefree in every support-minimal solution, and excludes all other supports, not merely a small numerical interval. The three integers themselves are not new, and no general claim about higher-support solutions is made.
